article.description: Our Vision, Logo & Values

article.title: NCLAT rejects Noida & Greater Noida authorities' plea for secured creditor status in Shubhkamna Buildtech case
article.description: The NCLAT has ruled against Noida and Greater Noida development authorities seeking secured creditor recognition in the Shubhkamna Buildtech insolvency matter, affirming the...
article.articleTextExcerpt: Regulatory 3 min read NCLAT rejects Noida & Greater Noida authorities' plea for secured creditor status in Shubhkamna Buildtech case The NCLAT has rejected the claims of Noida and Greater Noida authorities as secured creditors. article.title: Four AK-203 assault rifles among 12 weapons stolen from high-security Secunderabad Cantonment
article.description: Various army personnel, including a few Agniveers, have been questioned.
article.articleTextExcerpt: Twelve weapons, including four AK-203 assault rifles, seven pistols and an INSAS rifle, have been stolen from the high-security Secunderabad Cantonment near Hyderabad in Telangana. More than 1,000 rounds of ammunition and a pair of passive night-vision binoculars were also found stolen, according to defence sources. The incident came to light around 7:50 am on Monday. The arms were allegedly stolen from a store room on the premises of the 20 Madras Regiment. Police sources said the area is accessed mainly by military personnel. Following a complaint by top Army personnel, police registered a case on Monday under sections 331(4) and 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for trespassing and breaking in for theft of government property. “In view of the nature of the missing articles, particularly the service weapons and ammunition, there is a possibility of their unauthorised possession, misuse or movement,” the complaint read. “We have started the investigation with the full cooperation of the Army regiment,” a senior police officer said. Sharing details, Narinder Singh Bindra, president of the Gurdwara Sri Hemkund Sahib Management Trust, said snowfall began on the night of September 26. He said the pilgrimage was initially suspended for September 26 and 27. “The snow is now melting, but conditions in the high-altitude region remain severe, forcing us to keep the yatra on hold,” he said. article.articleTextExcerpt: Instant cameras have never really been about image quality, advanced controls, or getting the perfect shot. They are about taking a photo, hearing the motor whirr, and watching the image slowly roll out. The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 understands that better than most. At Rs 8,499, the Mini 13 does not reinvent the instant-camera experience. Most of it will feel familiar if you have used the Instax Mini 12, but Fujifilm has made a few small changes, including a mechanical self-timer, while keeping the camera simple enough for almost anyone to use. The result is an instant camera that prioritises the experience over technical precision. The Instax Mini 13 has a rounded, almost pillowy design that makes it clear this is not aimed at serious photographers. It is designed for parties, travel, casual snapshots and selfies, and the design fits that purpose well. It comes in five colours, Dreamy Purple, Frost Blue, Candy Pink, Lagoon Green, and Clay White. article.title: Mono Rail Projects
article.description: Guide to monorail in India — the Mumbai Monorail (MMRDA), how straddle-beam monorail works, shelved projects and the latest news.
article.articleTextExcerpt: A monorail runs on a single elevated beam rather than a conventional two-rail track. That makes it a compact, fully elevated mode, useful on dense urban corridors where road space is tight. In India the flagship is the Mumbai Monorail, the country’s first and so far only system. This page covers monorail in India: how the technology works, where it runs, and the latest developments. A monorail vehicle straddles or hangs from a single guideway beam, usually on rubber tyres. The result is a small footprint, a tight turning radius and a quiet ride. Most modern systems, Mumbai’s included, use the straddle-beam design, where the train sits astride a slim concrete beam. On capacity it sits below metro. It works well as a feeder or on medium-demand corridors, but it cannot match a metro’s throughput, which is why cities weigh it carefully against light metro and Metrolite. The Mumbai Monorail is India’s first and only monorail, running 19.54 km between Chembur and Sant Gadge Maharaj Chowk (Jacob Circle) under the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), serving eastern and central Mumbai neighbourhoods that the metro and suburban rail do not reach directly. article.articleTextExcerpt: Water metro systems bring metro-style public transport to India’s rivers, backwaters and harbours. They run modern, air-conditioned electric-hybrid boats on fixed routes and timetables, tied into metro and bus services through common ticketing. Kochi pioneered the idea, and cities across India are now studying and adopting it. This page follows India’s water metro projects: their routes, their operators and the latest developments. A water metro applies the discipline of urban rail to waterways. It runs dedicated terminals, level boarding, fixed high-frequency routes, smart-card and QR ticketing, and battery-electric or hybrid vessels built for low wake and low emissions. Rather than competing with a city’s metro, it stretches the network across water that road and rail cannot easily cross, joining islands, riverbanks and harbour districts into one integrated system. The Kochi Water Metro, run by Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL), is India’s first and largest system of its kind. Its electric-hybrid boats link islands around Kochi with the mainland and with the city’s metro network. A road commute that once took hours can drop to under an hour. Each corridor links to its full Metro Rail News profile with route, stations, cost and current status. A city metro handles short, frequent hops within an urban area and usually tops out near 80 km/h. High-speed rail, like the Mumbai to Ahmedabad bullet train, is built for 300-plus km/h intercity travel between distant cities. RRTS takes the middle ground on purpose. article.title: Semi-High-Speed Rail
article.description: Guide to India's semi-high-speed rail — Kerala SilverLine, Pune–Nashik & Ahmedabad–Rajkot corridors, Vande Bharat, speeds, status and latest news.
article.articleTextExcerpt: Semi-high-speed rail sits between conventional Indian Railways services and true 320 km/h high-speed rail. Think corridors and trains built for roughly 130 to 200 km/h. In India that covers both dedicated new semi-HSR corridors, such as the Kerala SilverLine and Pune to Nashik projects, and faster services on upgraded routes. This page follows India’s semi-high-speed rail corridors: their routes, their status and the latest developments. Each project links to its full Metro Rail News profile with route, cost and current status. Semi-HSR buys a big jump in journey speed without the cost and complexity of full high-speed rail. Where HSR needs entirely dedicated, grade-separated corridors for 320 km/h running, semi-HSR aims for 160 to 200 km/h. It gets there either on purpose-built standard-gauge corridors or by upgrading existing alignments, straightening curves, strengthening track and signalling, and fencing the right of way. For routes where demand and terrain do not yet justify a bullet train, it is the pragmatic option. Several states are chasing dedicated semi-high-speed corridors. article.title: Hyperloop Technology
article.description: Guide to hyperloop in India — the IIT Madras test track, Mumbai–Pune proposal, how hyperloop works, and the latest developments.
article.articleTextExcerpt: Hyperloop is an emerging ultra-high-speed transport concept. A levitating pod travels through a near-vacuum tube, cutting air resistance so far that speeds beyond 1,000 km/h become possible in theory, fast enough to turn an intercity trip into minutes. In India the technology is still at the research and test-track stage, driven by academic and railway efforts. This page covers hyperloop in India: how it works, where it stands, and the latest developments. A hyperloop system pulls together three ideas. A sealed tube is held at very low pressure to strip out most air resistance. A pod levitates on magnetic or air-bearing systems to remove rolling friction. Linear-motor propulsion then accelerates and brakes the pod. In principle that delivers airline-beating speed at ground level with high energy efficiency. The engineering is hard, though. Holding a vacuum over long distances, keeping passengers safe, managing thermal expansion of the tubes and controlling cost all remain unsolved at scale, which is why hyperloop everywhere is still pre-commercial. A metro serves travel within a city at up to 80–100 km/h with closely spaced stations. RRTS (Regional Rapid Transit System, branded Namo Bharat) is a 160 km/h semi-high-speed regional network built by NCRTC to connect cities 100–200 km apart with fewer stops. The 82.15 km Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut Namo Bharat corridor is fully operational since 22 February 2026, with 25 stations including the integrated Meerut Metro. It is India's first RRTS corridor. The Delhi–Gurugram–SNB–Alwar corridor (199 km) and Delhi–Sonipat–Panipat corridor (103 km) are approved under Phase 1, and a Ghaziabad–Noida International Airport (Jewar) link of about 72 km is proposed.

article.title: Building India: Land Markets Define the Next Development Frontier
article.description: As India's economy expands and infrastructure accelerates, land markets are increasingly influencing the geography of India’s next development cycle.
article.articleTextExcerpt: As India's economy expands and infrastructure accelerates, land markets are increasingly influencing the geography of India’s next development cycle. This report examines how the market is evolving and where the most promising opportunities are emerging for stakeholders across the real estate ecosystem. Our research spans 18,158 acres of land transactions across 33 cities between 2021 and Q1 2026. Beyond the scale of activity, these transactions represent an estimated 1.4 billion sq. ft. of development potential and approximately $176 billion in estimated development value, equivalent to broadly 22X the combined FY26 revenue of India's top 10 listed real estate companies. The report goes beyond transaction volumes to decode the strategies, corridors, asset classes and deal & capital structures shaping land activities, from the shift toward partnership-led models to the growing role of institutional capital. Whether your focus is high-growth micro-markets or large-scale commercial development, the findings offer a clear, data-backed view of where value is concentrating. article.title: India Data Centre Market H1 2026
article.description: India Data Centre Market Grows on Cloud, AI and Digital Adoption
article.articleTextExcerpt: India Data Centre Market Grows on Cloud, AI and Digital Adoption India’s data centre market continued its rapid expansion in H1 2026, reinforcing the country’s position as one of the fastest-growing digital infrastructure destinations in the Asia Pacific region. Driven by rising data consumption, cloud adoption, artificial intelligence workloads, and ongoing digital transformation initiatives, operational data centre capacity has expanded significantly over the past few years. Supported by strong investment activity and a robust development pipeline of nearly 3.9 GW, India is well positioned for the next phase of growth in data centre and AI infrastructure. Key Highlights from H1 2026 India is the third-largest data centre market in APAC by operational capacity. Operational data centre capacity reached nearly 1.8 GW, rising substantially from around 400 MW in 2019. Mumbai remains India's largest data centre market and one of the most significant hubs in the APAC region. Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi NCR continue to strengthen their position as major secondary data centre markets. India has a robust development pipeline of nearly 3.9 GW across under-construction and planned projects.

article.articleTextExcerpt: For Baldhir Singh Bhullar, a 35-year-old BBA graduate and a farmer by choice, two failed wheat sowings in a single season in 2021 became a turning point towards diversification — shifting him to vegetables in open fields and protected cultivation. Now, 13 acres under vegetables generate more than Rs 1 crore annually, compared to about Rs 75 lakh he used to get from 60 acres under wheat and paddy. A resident of Basti Nanaksar in Faridkot district, Bhullar had sown wheat on 25 acres in 2021 using a Crop Residue Management machine for the first time without burning stubble. The crop on 20 acres was attacked by a stem borer, forcing him to uproot it. He sowed wheat again, but within three days, heavy rain damaged the freshly sown crop. “After we faced heavy losses, my father wanted to lease out the land, but I had a different plan,” Bhullar said. He planted tomatoes on 13 of the 20 acres where the wheat crop was destroyed. article.articleTextExcerpt: The recently concluded National Family Health Survey-6 (NFHS-6) has revealed a worrying trend in Ludhiana district. It has brought forward that the proportion of households consuming iodised salt has dropped from 94.9 per cent in the last survey to 88.7 per cent. Iodised salt is a critical source of iodine, a trace mineral required for the production of thyroid hormones that regulate growth, metabolism and development. Public health experts warn that the decline in usage could reverse decades of progress made under India’s Universal Salt Iodisation (USI) programme, which was introduced to combat iodine deficiency disorders. The growing popularity of sendha namak (rock salt) and other speciality variants has contributed to the decline. “While these alternatives are often marketed as ‘natural’ or ‘pure’ but they lack adequate iodine content. Sendha namak may be used occasionally, but relying on it exclusively for daily cooking deprives the body of essential iodine,” said Dipti, a nutritionist. Lifestyle electric two-wheeler maker Creatara Mobility on Wednesday opened its first manufacturing plant in Faridabad, with an installed annual capacity of 30,000 units. article.description: The Union Cabinet has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme to strengthen intra-state transmission systems and support the evacuation of up to 135 GW of...
article.articleTextExcerpt: The Union Cabinet has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme to strengthen intra-state transmission systems and support the evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy across states and union territories. The scheme, targeted for completion by FY 2032-33, has a total outlay of Rs 1.86 trillion. Of the total outlay, Rs 1.36 trillion will be allocated for intra-state transmission infrastructure, while Rs 500 billion will be used to deploy 50 GWh of battery energy storage systems. The storage capacity will be deployed at renewable energy developer or generator locations and other grid locations to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and non-solar hour demand. The scheme provides central financial support of Rs 540.82 billion to help offset intra-state transmission charges and reduce the cost of renewable power. Greenfield transmission projects will be implemented through tariff-based competitive bidding, while brownfield upgrades and network strengthening will follow the cost-plus basis.

article.description: Dramatic CCTV footage shows panic and a cloud of dust and smoke around the vehicle; police investigating reason for the blast.
article.articleTextExcerpt: A car being refuelled with compressed natural gas (CNG) exploded without warning at a fuel station on National Highway-48 near Karjan in Vadodara district of Gujarat, showering a large area with debris and shattered glass, leaving two nearby vehicles badly damaged, and triggering a wave of panic among fuel station staff, customers, and bystanders. No one was, however, injured in the explosion that took place on Thursday (October 1) afternoon. The driver of the vehicle had stepped out of it as it was being refuelled, thus averting a potentially serious accident at the station which is usually busy. Under safety rules enforced by regulatory authorities such as the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board, it is mandatory for occupants of a CNG vehicle to step out of the vehicle when it is being refuelled. This is because CNG is typically filled into the vehicle’s cylinders at a very high pressure of 200-220 bar, which is 20-40 times higher than a domestic cooking gas (LPG) cylinder, and 70-100 times the pressure of a car tyre. According to the RBI, latest data reported by authorised dealer banks show that FCNR(B) deposits mobilised under the facility stood at $132.98 billion, while Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) brought in $5.32 billion and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) $5.296 billion. The facility, introduced by the central bank on June 8, was aimed at encouraging fresh foreign currency inflows into the banking system, strengthening the country’s external buffers and supporting domestic liquidity. Under the arrangement, banks could mobilise fresh three-to-five-year FCNR(B) deposits and swap the foreign currency with the RBI at a concessional rate, thus reducing hedging cost for banks. article.articleTextExcerpt: Even as rainfall in some parts of the country eased the pressure on electricity demand recently, coal stocks at domestic coal-based power plants have continued to slide, dipping by nearly 24% from the level recorded at the beginning of September. The depletion in coal stocks comes amid an unusual surge in electricity demand this September, and greater reliance on coal-based generation as hydropower output has declined due to deficient rainfall and El Niño-influenced weather conditions. Peak power demand has also remained close to the levels seen during the summer peak, touching 269 gigawatts (GW) on September 10 — the highest ever recorded for September and just 1 GW below the year’s peak of 270 GW seen in May. As of September 27, coal stocks at domestic coal-based power plants stood at 19.2 million tonnes (mt), 64% below the required stock of 53.7 mt. The stock was at 25.4 mt on September 1, when it was 52.5% below the required stock of 53.5 mt. Coal stocks have declined by more than half compared with the year-ago period. With a total outlay of Rs 1,86,405 crore, the scheme is targeted for completion by FY33. This scheme is aimed at tackling a festering problem in India’s power sector — even as the peak power demand has been surging to record highs, the grid operators have been forced to curtail electricity generated by solar power sources due to transmission bottlenecks. Along with the development of the intra-state transmission system (InSTS), the scheme, for the first time under the Green Energy Corridor programme, includes a dedicated battery energy storage component, with provisions for deploying 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at renewable energy developer/generator sites or other locations of importance to the grid. According to the government, the storage capacity is intended to address intermittency, transmission congestion and peak-hour curtailment, while helping meet demand during non-solar hours. article.title: Congress rejigs UP unit ahead of 2027 Assembly polls; Aradhana Misra gets PCC chief’s post
article.description: The Congress on Friday changed the guard in Uttar Pradesh, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as Pradesh Congress Committee president and...
article.articleTextExcerpt: The Congress on Friday changed the guard in Uttar Pradesh, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as Pradesh Congress Committee president and appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president, in a significant organisational rejig months ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The party also appointed Devinder Nishad and Alok Prasad as senior vice-presidents and named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as the new Leader of the Congress Legislature Party in the state. article.articleTextExcerpt: Two fighters of the Indian AIR Force, a Tejas and a Su-30MKI, fly in formation. (Image credit: IAF) The Indian Air Force (IAF) chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh delivered a blunt assessment of the fighter shortage plaguing his organisation. The reduction in numbers has been eroding the effectiveness of the force for years and shows no sign of easing soon. Speaking in New Delhi ahead of the 94th Air Force Day, Singh said the IAF's current fighter fleet stands at 29 fighter squadrons against a sanctioned strength of 42.5, and that the force needs to induct 36 to 40 new aircraft annually to meet its current requirements. This totals effectively to the induction of two fighter squadrons every year just to arrest the decline. "There is some extra delay, and there is no doubt that it is going to hurt us," he said, pointing squarely at the slow pace of fighter inductions.A significant portion of this delay traces back to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's production of the Tejas Mark-1A. article.description: Delays of up to 859 days in tender processes for replacing old and damaged water and sewer pipelines in Indores Bhagirathpura contributed to the contaminated drinking water...
article.articleTextExcerpt: Delays of up to 859 days in tender processes for replacing old and damaged water and sewer pipelines in Indore's Bhagirathpura contributed to the contaminated drinking water tragedy in the area, a judicial commission has concluded. The tragedy, which claimed several lives, could have been prevented had the pipeline replacement work been completed on time, it noted. The one-member commission headed by former Madhya Pradesh High Court Judge Sushil Kumar Gupta made the observations in its more than 600-page final report submitted to the HC, which had appointed the panel to probe the deaths linked to consumption of contaminated drinking water in Bhagirathpura in India's cleanest city. The commission found serious delays in key tenders for replacing damaged pipelines and laying new ones, attributing them to red tape and administrative laxity in the Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC). Speaking after inaugurating the Mukhyamantri Sugam Parivahan Seva and PM e-Bus Sewa in Bhopal, Gadkari said E20 petrol has been used in India since 2022 and is now being used in around four crore two-wheelers. Gadkari said the government was pursuing multiple alternatives to conventional fossil fuels. These include 100% ethanol-powered flex-fuel vehicles, electric vehicles and hydrogen-powered buses and trucks. article.articleTextExcerpt: A few years ago, my father and I boarded a train for Bhopal. I had an important examination there. My mind, however, was already at the examination centre. My father had decided to accompany me. He was excited to see Bhopal, its lakes, its greenery and, most importantly, to try the local food. I was happy to have him with me, but underneath I was worried. What if I did not perform well? What if my anxiety spoiled the journey for him? But Bhopal slowly took my mind elsewhere. We reached Bhopal and the first thing we noticed was how clean and orderly the station was. There was a sweetness in the way people spoke and lived their lives. It made me slow down. Then came the food. Hot poha, jalebi, dhokla, Bhopali paan and Bhopali chai. Nothing extraordinary, perhaps, but sitting with my father, putting my worries aside and eating without thinking about the examination felt strangely comforting. We visited the Upper and Lower Lakes. We sat there for nearly an hour, looking at the pristine water, flotilla of white swans and the clouded blue sky. The submission by MoCA was in response to a query from PPPAC chair and Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur in an August 4 meeting on the planned privatisation of 11 airports — clubbed into five bundles — for a 50-year period. The panel gave its in-principle approval to the proposal, as per the minutes of the meeting. Thakur had sought the ministry’s response on what measures were envisaged to ensure that the risks related to concentration and over-leveraging are minimised, given the oligopolistic nature of the aviation sector. The PPPAC, under the Department of Economic Affairs, is responsible for appraisal and approval of central sector public private partnership (PPP) projects exceeding Rs 100 crore. article.articleTextExcerpt: Logistics 6 min read Zero-emission freight will need more than new trucks India’s freight transition starts before electrification: cut empty kilometres, shift long-haul cargo to rail and water, and build the data needed to measure progress. Nikhil Agarwal ETManufacturing Published On Sep 7, 2026 at 03:12 PM IST The industry conversation has narrowed almost entirely to one of them: when diesel trucks will be replaced by electric or hydrogen ones.About 3 per cent of the vehicles on Indian roads produce close to half of the country’s road transport emissions. Those vehicles are medium and heavy-duty trucks, and almost all of them still run on diesel.That is an unusual shape for an emissions problem, and a useful one. The emissions sit in a narrow, identifiable set of assets, owned and hired by a countable set of operators, financiers and cargo owners. A relatively small number of commercial decisions can move the number. With road already carrying close to 70 per cent of India’s freight, and manufacturing and export growth set to add volume rather than reduce it, those decisions are worth getting right. According to data provided by the Chandigarh Police, of the 29 enrolled, 14 inmates have opted for woodwork and 15—including nine men and six women—have chosen sewing. article.articleTextExcerpt: Some of the most perfect mornings of my young life belonged to Chandigarh in winter. They began before the city had properly awakened, when the air was crisp, the dawn sky still pale, and the world seemed to belong only to those willing to rise early. I would wake up with an almost childlike excitement, knowing that we were going for a walk along the forest path by Sukhna Lake. We would set out bundled against the cold, carrying a breakfast of packed sandwiches and warm paranthas for later. There was something wonderfully ceremonial about these walks. As we entered the forest, the familiar city seemed to fall away, replaced by the whisper of leaves, the cool fragrance of winter, and the cheerful chorus of birds. Their melodious chirping was sometimes so beautiful that we would stop simply to listen. Sukhna Lake in those early hours was a different world from the lake of the evenings. Instead of bustling with people, it lay calm and unhurried, morning light shimmering on its still waters. In places where moss and algae carpeted its surface, my brother and I would gleefully pick up stones and toss them into the water, watching the moss tremble and give way as ripples spread outward.

Their study was published in the Journal of Threatened Taxa on May 26 this year. The first snake was found inside a gaushala on August 19, 2025. Another was found in the courtyard of a house at Sunda Ki Dhani on September 12 and the third near an under-construction house at Rukansar on September 21 last year. article.description: India is expected to experience its weakest monsoon season in 17 years as a strengthening El Nino curbs rainfall and raises concerns over crop yields and food inflation.
article.articleTextExcerpt: India is expected to experience its weakest monsoon season in 17 years as a strengthening El Nino curbs rainfall and raises concerns over crop yields and food inflation. Cumulative rainfall during the June-to-September monsoon season is currently running 15% below the long-term average, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The initial forecast was just a 10% shortfall back in May. If the deficit holds, this would be the weakest monsoon since 2009, when rainfall was 18% below normal, said Christian Werner of Australia-based consultancy Global Weather Climate Analytics. A potential tropical cyclone could form in the Bay of Bengal in the final week of September, potentially easing the shortfall in eastern and northeastern India, he said, adding that the storm was unlikely to significantly shift the national picture, with the seasonal deficit expected to settle between 13% and 16%. The lack of rain threatens both current harvests and the next planting cycle, adding pressure on food prices that have already risen for seven straight months. For a country that has steadily expanded its medal base across disciplines, Aichi-Nagoya offered a mix of progress and reminders of the gaps that remain. The approach differs from the Construction and Development Agency (C&DA) model used for several major Mhada projects. Under the C&DA structure, a private developer finances and constructs the project on Mhada land, transfers a portion of the completed flats to the authority for lottery allotments and sells most of the remaining homes. Motilal Nagar, Abhyudaya Nagar, Bandra Reclamation, Adarsh Nagar and GTB Nagar were developed through that route. Pratiksha Nagar comprises 216 buildings and nearly 10,000 homes. About 90 buildings have been used as transit accommodation over several decades, while the remaining buildings house beneficiaries who received homes through Mhada lotteries. Form 132 has also been amended to include transfers of immovable property by a non-resident to a resident individual or HUF. Buyers will have to provide the property address and type, the names and Permanent Account Numbers of buyers, and each buyer’s proportion of the sale consideration. Details required for a non-resident seller include the name, PAN where available, status, contact number, email address and overseas address. July’s decline came alongside a shift towards lower-risk products, while small-cap and mid-cap schemes continued to attract money. The mutual fund industry’s net assets under management (AUM) rose to Rs 87.07 lakh crore in August from Rs 85.75 lakh crore in July, an increase of about 1.5%. article.description: Explore Prateek Grand City in Siddharth Vihar, a 40-acre integrated township in Ghaziabad with green spaces, amenities, retail and community infrastructure.
article.articleTextExcerpt: There is a point at which a residential project stops feeling like a collection of apartment towers and starts functioning more like a neighbourhood. At Prateek Grand City, that point is 40 acres. Located in Siddharth Vihar, Ghaziabad, the development was planned as a 40-acre integrated township, bringing residences, landscaped greens, recreation, retail convenience and social infrastructure together within one larger plan. That scale matters. In a standalone residential development, most of the planning naturally revolves around the apartment and the amenities immediately around it. In a township, the question becomes wider: what does everyday life look like once thousands of people begin living in the same place? Where do children play? Where do residents meet? What happens when someone needs something for the house? How much of daily life can happen without repeatedly stepping outside the community? Prateek Grand City was designed around those questions. Today, with thousands of families making the township their home, it also offers a useful example of how Siddharth Vihar real estate has evolved from simply adding housing inventory to creating larger residential ecosystems. Building at that scale using the same manual, site-heavy methods we have relied on for decades simply does not work.The immediate catalyst for change is labour. article.title: VOC Port records 74.5% rise in wind turbine blade handling in April-August

candidates.title: Delhi-NCR sees 16% drop in new home launches; Gurgaon leads supply
candidates.description: JLL says Delhi-NCR home sales slowed in Q2 as cautious buyers held back, while property prices and rents continued to rise.
candidates.articleTextExcerpt: Residential sales in Delhi-NCR moderated in the second quarter as cautious homebuying sentiment weighed on demand, although prices and rents continued to rise, according to JLL. A total of 10,021 residential units were sold during Q2, down 9% year-on-year. Gurgaon accounted for the largest share at 43%, with demand concentrated along Dwarka Expressway, Golf Course Extension Road, New Gurgaon and Manesar. Noida represented 36% of overall sales, followed by Ghaziabad at 18%. JLL said sales momentum remained healthy in Ghaziabad, Faridabad and Delhi, supported by a steady flow of new projects that attracted buyers seeking newer housing products. Residential launches also declined, with more than 11,250 units launched during the quarter, down 16% year-on-year. Gurgaon accounted for 45% of new supply, followed by Ghaziabad at 30% and Noida at 17%. Delhi and Faridabad recorded quarterly increases in new supply. New launches were concentrated along established growth corridors, particularly Dwarka Expressway in Gurgaon and NH-24 in Ghaziabad.
